rationale: B wins because it has better editorial restraint: "Allbirds shrinks its way to a first margin gain, but the losses haven't stopped" puts the strongest facts into one skeptical, sellable story instead of letting every fact become its own pitch. A is strong, but "The prevailing belief in DTC retail is that growth comes from expanding the range and the store footprint" imports an unsupported category thesis and makes the assortment angle feel close to its margin angle. B's partner-led wholesale story is also cleaner than A's more company-centered channel pivot.
gaps_in_A: "The prevailing belief in DTC retail is that growth comes from expanding the range and the store footprint" is not in the update. That's a useful hypothesis, not a supplied fact.
"a brand that built itself on direct retail is leaning on someone else's shelves" imports outside Allbirds history and assumes shelf mechanics before the partner and deal scope are known.
"durability is the chronic knock against natural-material shoes" is plausible beat context, but it is not grounded in the supplied facts. Prove it or strip it.

"Allbirds bet its comeback on fewer shoes, not more" risks being a duplicate of the margin-turnaround angle unless the company can prove the range cut, not just the broader turnaround, drove the margin change.
gaps_in_B: "The retailer betting shelf space" and "committing floor space" assume physical retail placement before the partner name, door count, channel, or in-store timing are supplied.
"The story runs best when the product reaches the partner's stores" invents a timing milestone. Useful if true, but the update does not say when or how the partnership goes live.
"what is the cash position?" is a fair markets diligence question, but it is not in the supplied update. Keep it framed as a hole to fill, not a pitch fact.

B folds the 40% range cut into the margin angle and skips a standalone assortment/merchandising trade angle. That restraint is mostly good, but it leaves one plausible retail-strategy pitch underdeveloped.
